verses.verse:
हस्तार्ध परिमिता तारी मध्या हस्तैक मानका।
सार्धहस्ता भवेन्मन्द्रा द्विहस्ताऽपि क्वचित।७८।
verses.text: The Tārī (small, high-pitched flute) measures half a hasta (cubit), the Madhyā (medium flute) one hasta; the Mandrā (large, low-pitched flute) should be one and a half hastas, and sometimes even two hastas.

commentary.text: It is a proof of the Supreme Lord's wondrous glory that whatever is good for a creature is also what it likes. So animals and birds give up food when they are sick. So in childhood there is a natural liking for the Tārī flute (of the high octave), and in youth for the Madhyā flute (of the middle octave). This too is a special feature of the flute. If the placement of the fingers is to be kept up, it will be best to practise on a small flute from childhood. In the above śloka the dimensions of all three flutes are given. The Tārī flute is half a hasta (cubit) long, the Madhyā one hasta long and the Mandra one and a half hastas long. Here and there, practitioners with long fingers even play a flute two hastas long.

subsection.title: Practice of the Tongue and of the Fingers

terms.en: small (high-pitched) flute, half a hasta long
